experiment.label: reasoning-full75
experiment.description: Full-benchmark replication of E05 reasoning-on treatment (population Pareto; CI comparison vs E05). max_tokens 48k->64k: cap never bound on healthy E05 responses; qwen-35b ceiling 81920.

judge_details.family_stake_note: Non-candidate family (Anthropic judge, non-Anthropic candidates) → self-preference bias is structurally absent by v1 design.

config.generation_deadline_basis: 2 x p99 (nearest-rank) of 69 frozen-treatment generation calls from E04/E05 logs (p99=1014.6s, qwen-9b/CIF-024), floor 900s -> 2030s; scaled by 64k/48k token budget and rounded -> 2700s (2026-07-08)

run_notes: Full-benchmark replication of E05's reasoning-on treatment: all 75 prompts (no sampling), reasoning=true, temp 0.6, provider sort=throughput, dual judges — the adequately-powered frozen-config run every synthesis since E04 has requested.

One deliberate treatment deviation vs E05: max_tokens 48000->64000. The 48k cap never bound on a healthy E05 response (59/60 finished stop; max healthy ~27k tokens), so this is behaviorally identical treatment with headroom; qwen-35b's provider ceiling is 81920 completion tokens.
GENERATION_DEADLINE_S raised 2030->2700 to match the bigger budget: a run-to-cap repetition loop should be STORED (finish_reason=length, diagnosable) rather than deadline-aborted into an error.

E05's 20 prompts are nested in this run (sampler prefix-stability verified): shared-20 is a repeat-draw A/A cut, disjoint-55 a fresh-sample cut; CI/rank comparison written by scripts/stability_analysis.py to runs/E07-reasoning-full75/stability_analysis.json.

Machine synthesis compares vs E06-temp06-3p (predecessor rule picks the highest prior experiment number); the E05 comparison — the one under test — is carried by the stability script and the run report.

Analysis-tab override (2026-07-10, manual via Claude Code, not the diagnose API): the committed synthesis was reconciled to its protocol predecessor E05 (E06 was a side-branch temp=0.6/reasoning=false n=3 probe, not E05's successor). synthesis.json now carries predecessor=E05 plus an analysis_override provenance block; the machine's E06 comparison above records only what the auto-rule did.

Reasoning on/off drill (E05 rec 3 / E06 rec 2) deliberately declined: Qwen3.5 is a thinking family and reasoning-on is the deployment-relevant mode; the degenerate-output question is addressed by the sidecar probe (runs/E07-reasoning-full75/probe/).

Retry-policy heterogeneity (ruling 2026-07-10, mid-experiment): 220 responses came from the original policy (empty completions retried up to 5x); the last 5 items (CIF-019/023/057/062 x qwen-9b, CIF-058 x qwen-35b — persistent runaway-CoT loopers, ~25 discarded runaway streams in the main pass) were completed under the new loop-terminal policy: a looping empty draw is stored as a flagged loop_failure record and graded 0/N mechanically. Loops count as failures even when escaped; see decode_health in results and meta/RESULTS_SCHEMA.md 3.2.
⚠ Empty candidate response(s) stored for qwen-9b/CIF-057 — their prompts are excluded from comparison; regenerate.
⚠ Judge claude-fable-5: 712 × judge_refusal — affected criteria count as FAIL.
All judges graded the same candidate responses (single generation pass), so judge columns are directly comparable.
Judges reason with adaptive thinking over a streamed 32000-token budget; candidate reasoning enabled at temperature 0.6.

prompts.prompt_text:
1 week rota for my employees for 15th-21st December 2025, I have 2 FT (26-34 hour per week) and 4 PT employees (16-24 hours per week). Full-time employees are Maria and Nuria, part-time employees are Nate, Jack, Ben, and Finn. We are a bar closing at late times so the shifts are 16:00-22:00, 16:00-23:00, 18:00-01:00, 19:00-01:00, 1 person per shift for Thursday-Sunday inclusive. Monday-Tuesday shifts are 16:00-21:00, 16:00-23:00, 17:00-23:00. We are closed on Wednesdays. It's coming up to Christmas holiday season so I'm having trouble making this rota around my employees booked days off. Can you make this rota? 

Full-time employees are also senior staff, so I need at least one FTer to work the closing shift to cash-up every night we are open (the PTers aren't trained to do this). Also, Nate and Jack who joined us for this holiday period are both under-18 so they can't handle alcohol alone, don't schedule either of them unless there is at least one adult working at the same time. Maria has a family event on Friday, so don't schedule her any shifts that day, and on Sundays, she needs to finish before midnight because buses don't run late. Ben goes to university so can't do shifts starting at 16:00 on the weekdays, 17:00 and after is okay. 

Don't schedule FT staff to work more than 5 days in total, and PT shouldn't work more than 4 days in total, this is in their contracts. I want to be a good employer, so I want the PTers to have at least 2 consecutive days off (including our closed Wednesday), it would be annoying if they had to come in to work every other day. I need the total hours for each employee for this week to calculate payroll, FT are on £16.5 per hour, Nate and Jack who are only with us for this seasonal rush are on £14 per hour, Ben and Finn who are our regular PTers are on £14.5 per hour, sum up each employee's total hours at the end.

prompts.prompt_text: I'm trying to make a release schedule for a podcast that I am on the committee for. It's been tough because I don't know if we have a diverse enough set of episodes that we recorded so far, and we don't want two similar episodes back-to-back. It's a podcast for trumpet players, interviewing trumpet players. We don't want two women back-to-back or two non-Americans back-to-back just to keep things interesting and diverse. I feel like we have too many American men to make that possible, but we also want to separate people who have the same job and people who talked about the same topics in their episode. Tom H. was great, an American man who is an orchestral player, and he talked about mindset and wellness which was cool. Matilda L. is from the UK, and she talked about being a soloist (because she's a soloist). Karen D., from Canada is an orchestral player, and she talked about being a woman in our industry. David H. is an American orchestral player, and he talked about the history of our organization. Jason D. is an American pedagogue and freelance musician, and he talked about the history of our organization, as did Ryan G, who shares the same career and nationality. Tine H. is a Norwegian soloist and chamber musician, and she talked about her struggles with cancer and how it affected her playing. Ashley H. is an American orchestral player, soloist, wellness coach, and pedagogue, and she talked about wellness. Sam B. is from France, and he is an orchestral player who talked about the audition circuit. Summer C. is American, and she talked about freelancing as a jazz musician, she is a jazz/ commercial player. Wiff R. is an American pedagogue who talked about building a vibrant and welcoming studio environment. Wayne B. is an American commercial player, and he talked about being a studio player in Los Angeles. We also want to release episodes every Monday beginning the first week in January, 2026, but we do not want to release any episodes on United States federal holidays. I don't know what to do, I need help here.

prompts.prompt_text:
Below are my notes about Homeostatic Regulation for my Health and Disease class. Can you please help me make flashcards to study the material for an upcoming test? I need to know everything, so please don’t omit any details. Also, please don’t present the information in bullet points since it will be easier to copy and paste them into my quiz program without them. For words or phrases that have an explicit definition (usually preceded by a colon), please just use the word or phrase as the question. For example – “Homeostasis” is the question and “the integrative action of the systems of an organism that result in the maintenance of the optimal internal environment despite variations in the external conditions” is the answer. For examples of feedback systems, you can just put the entire thing on one card since they’re all tied together. Other than examples (including the feedback system examples and dashes that start with “ex:”) or lists (like the levels of organization of the body), please put every dash or bullet point on a separate flashcard. For information that is presented in standalone sentences, please word the question as a natural question. For example – “Homeostasis is controlled through negative feedback” could use the question of “How is homeostasis controlled?” and the answer of “Homeostasis is controlled through negative feedback”. Sometimes you might have to incorporate the header into the question in order for it to make sense on its own, like “properties of produced messages” would need to be mentioned with “nervous system” in order for me to understand that the question is about properties of messages produced by the nervous system. Please bold the question and leave the answers in regular font.  
HOMEOSTATIC REGULATION
Levels of the organization of the body: 
•	Chemical or molecular levels
•	Cellular level
•	Tissue level
•	Organ level 
There are eleven organ systems in the human body, and intercommunication exists between them all.
Homeostasis: the integrative action of the systems of an organism that result in the maintenance of the optimal internal environment despite variations in the external conditions
•	Homeostatic regulation is the adjustment of physiological systems to preserve homeostasis
•	Homeostasis is controlled through negative feedback
Blood levels of glucose is an example of homeostatic regulation.
•	Any time there is a meal there is a peak in blood sugar.
•	Any carbohydrates that are consumed are broken down, solubilized, and enter the blood. We can measure this concentration change.
•	Disease can be monitored using this trend. People who have a challenge in glucose metabolism (diabetics) have larger peaks.
Mechanisms of homeostatic regulation:
1.	Autoregulation: intrinsic regulation
•	Activities of cell, tissue, organ, organ system change when faced with environmental variation
•	Ex: oxygen to cells
2.	Extrinsic regulation
•	Via the nervous and endocrine system
•	Control activities of many organ systems
•	Ex: exercise and oxygen use
A receptor, control center, and an effector are needed for homeostatic regulation.
•	Receptor: a sensor that is sensitive to a particular variable or stimulus
•	Control center: integration center, receives and processes information supplied by the receptor
•	Effector: a cell or organ that responds to the commands of the control center and whose activity opposes (negative feedback) or enhances (positive feedback) the stimulus
Body temperature regulation: example of a negative feedback system
•	Homeostasis: normal body temperature (37 degrees)
•	Stimulus: body temperature rises, normal temperature disturbed
•	Receptors: temperature sensors in skin and hypothalamus
•	Control center: thermoregulatory center in brain
•	Effectors: receives signal from the brain to cause sweat glands in skin to increase secretion and blood vessels in skin to dilate
•	Response: increased heat loss, body temperature drops, normal temperature restored
•	Internal fluctuations are smaller than environmental fluctuations (36.7-37.2)
Positive feedback
•	Rarely encountered
•	Tends to produce extreme results
•	Initial stimulus produces a response that exaggerates or enhances effects
•	Positive feedback loops are encountered when a potentially dangerous or stressful process must be completed quickly before homeostasis can be restored
Blood clotting response: example of a positive feedback system
•	Break in blood vessel wall causes bleeding
•	Damaged cells release chemicals
•	Clotting begins
•	Additional chemicals released, clotting accelerates
•	Blood clot plugs break in vessel wall; bleeding stops
•	The clotting response encourages the occurrence of more clotting.
•	When blood loss occurs, blood pressure and heart rate lowers because the body responds first to stop the bleeding and then it restores blood pressure.
Clotters: the nervous and endocrine system
•	The nervous and endocrine systems are the major homeostatic control systems of the body
•	Neuron
-	Stimulus induces (1) permeability increase, (2) Na+ and Ca2+ influx, (3) depolarization 
-	Secretion follows (1) depolarization, (2) permeability increase, (3) Ca2+ influx
-	Neurons that pass signals between each other are physically close
•	Simple endocrine cell: releases a signal into the blood, as generally mediated by calcium, and the signal can often travel farther and last longer.
Properties of produced messages
•	Nervous system: very private, very fast transmission (ms), very short message length (ms)
•	Endocrine system: less private, slow transmission (s), long message length (s, min, hr, days, weeks, etc)
Homeostasis at the cellular level is maintained through the action of cell membranes that maintain cell integrity, control cell activities, and have electrical activity that lead cell to cell signalling.
A fluid membrane surrounds our cells.
•	Membrane composition can vary
•	Integral proteins: serve as passive transport pores and channels, active-transport pumps and carriers, membrane-linked enzymes, and chemical signal receptors
•	Peripheral proteins: membrane-linked, do not extend through the membrane
•	Glycoproteins: have oligosaccharide side chains that are vital for cell recognition, interactions, adhesion, and communication
Intracellular signals are coordinated.

9.  **Sleep:** Never sacrifice sleep for study time. If you are tired, your Math performance will drop. Stick to the 10 PM bedtime.

### Study Tips for Your GED Tests

**1. Math Strategy**
*   **Calculator:** The GED math test allows a specific calculator (TI-30XS). Practice using it thoroughly. Know how to use the square root, fractions, and memory functions.
*   **Formulas:** You will be provided with a formula sheet, but memorize the most common ones (area of circles, perimeter, Pythagorean theorem) so you don't waste time looking them up.
*   **Units:** Always check the units in the question (inches vs. feet, cm vs. m).
*   **Time Management:** Do not get stuck on one question. Mark it and move on.

**2. Science Strategy**
*   **Passage First:** Read the question first, then read the passage. This helps you know what information to look for.
*   **Graphs:** Learn to interpret graphs and charts quickly. Look at the labels on the X and Y axes.
*   **Vocabulary:** Know the difference between independent and dependent variables.

**3. Time Management**
*   **Pomodoro Technique:** If you feel overwhelmed, study for 25 minutes and take a 5-minute break.
*   **Sleep:** Do not sacrifice sleep for studying. Your brain needs sleep to retain the information you are learning. Stick to the 8-hour goal.
*   **Hydration:** Drink water while studying. Dehydration causes brain fog.

**4. Test Taking**
*   **Read Carefully:** GED questions often include words like "NOT," "EXCEPT," or "LEAST." Circle these words.
*   **Eliminate Answers:** If you don't know the answer, eliminate the obviously wrong ones first to increase your odds of guessing correctly.
*   **Review:** If you have time left at the end of the test, review your answers, but only change them if you are sure you made a mistake.

Good luck! You have a solid plan. Stick to it.

### GED Study Tips

**Math Strategies**
*   **Use the Calculator:** The GED allows you to use a TI-30XS calculator for most of the math test. Learn how to use it efficiently (fractions, exponents, square roots) before test day.

*   **Plug in Answers:** For multiple-choice algebra questions, try plugging the answer choices back into the equation to see which one works.
*   **Focus on Weaknesses:** Spend 80% of your study time on the math topics you find hardest (e.g., algebra vs. geometry).

**General Test Taking**
*   **Read Carefully:** Social Studies and Science questions often have answers that can be found directly in the provided text or graphs. Don't rely on outside knowledge; rely on the material given.
*   **Manage Time:** Don't get stuck on one question. If you are unsure, flag it, move on, and come back if you have time.
*   **Sleep:** Do not sacrifice sleep for extra studying the night before a test. Your brain needs rest to recall information.
*   **Environment:** Ensure your testing area is quiet, well-lit, and free from distractions for your online exams.

I received this feedback from the client on the landing page copy we just sent for approval:

General Thoughts:

Make sure to use "Niagara-on-the-Lake" consistently throughout the copy, not just "Niagara." It’s important and needs to be accurate everywhere.

The wording could use a little more urgency. “Book now” works, but maybe something like “Limited time offer!” or “Hurry, spots are filling up fast!” would make it feel a bit more exclusive.

Icewine Time Copy:

"There’s no time like Icewine time in Niagara!" – This comes off as too cheesy. A more straightforward approach would be better, like: “January is the best time to experience Icewine in Niagara-on-the-Lake.”

"Let us pamper you..." feels a bit too casual. Maybe try something like: “Indulge in a luxurious winter getaway” or “Experience a true winter retreat.” It would sound a bit more refined.

The Icewine martini feels a little forced. It doesn’t really capture the essence of what people come to Niagara for. A focus on the actual Icewine would be better. For example: “Enjoy locally crafted Icewine paired with a delicious charcuterie plate” would feel more in line with the experience.

Christmas Wonderland Garden Copy:

"This holiday discover the Christmas Wonderland Garden in Niagara!" – Don’t forget it should be Niagara-on-the-Lake. That’s important to get right.

The description of the garden sounds great, but it could use a little more magic. For instance, instead of “transformed The Gardens at Pillar and Post,” you might say, “Transformed The Gardens at Pillar and Post into a sparkling holiday wonderland.” This feels a little more festive and inviting.

The phrase "exclusive inclusions for hotel guests" feels a little stiff. A more natural alternative could be “exclusive perks for hotel guests” or “extra holiday experiences for guests.” It’s simpler and clearer.

The holiday movies under the stars could use more detail. Maybe mention specific movies or describe the experience a little more. Something like “holiday classics under the stars” might sound better than just “holiday movies.”

Wine Country Winter Getaway Copy:

"Embrace the season with an escape to wine country!" – This is fine, but it’s a bit overused. Maybe a more specific option like: “Escape to the serene beauty of Niagara-on-the-Lake wine country this winter” would feel more unique.

The sentence about outdoors or snuggling up could be tighter. Instead of: “Whether you love the great outdoors, or are looking to settle in, snuggle up and unwind…” try: “Whether you want outdoor adventure or a cozy retreat, Niagara-on-the-Lake is perfect for winter getaways.” It reads a bit smoother.

"Specialty coffee" feels too generic. Something like “handcrafted coffee” or “a signature winter drink” could sound more special and in line with the luxury experience.

The note about “(Some blackout dates apply)” feels out of place in the middle of the copy. It might be better to save that for the terms or fine print, so it doesn’t break up the flow.

---

Can you update the landing page copy below to reflect the client's change requests? Only make changes for points that are written in the imperative (e.g. "change X to Y", "update this"), otherwise leave it as is. For any remaining points, write a short rebuttal (one bullet point per point of feedback) that explains why we are choosing to keep the original copy. Put these bullet points in a separate section from the revised copy.

Here is the copy pre-client feedback:

There’s no time like Icewine time in Niagara! AVAILABLE JANUARY 1 – 31, 2026 January is Niagara’s world-renowned ice grape harvest season which makes it the perfect time to taste your way through wineries and local events celebrating this rich and delicious Canadian wine. Let us pamper you with a getaway that includes luxurious accommodations plus a shared charcuterie plate to be enjoyed while sipping a specialty Icewine martini. Book now with promo code: ICEWINE

This holiday discover the Christmas Wonderland Garden in Niagara! AVAILABLE DECEMBER 1, 2025 – JANUARY 3, 2026* We’ve transformed The Gardens at Pillar and Post into a true seasonal Christmas wonderland complete with sparkling lights, holiday music, festive snacks, an ice rink, warming fire pits and holiday movies under the stars. With exclusive inclusions for hotel guests this signature package comes with a little extra holiday cheer (see full list below). Wonderful holiday memories await you in Niagara-on-the-Lake this Christmas season! Book now with promo code: WONDER

Embrace the season with an escape to wine country! AVAILABLE NOVEMBER 16, 2025 – MARCH 31, 2026* Whether you love the great outdoors, or are looking to settle in, snuggle up and unwind, Niagara-on-the-Lake is the perfect place to warm up to winter. Your winter getaway includes overnight accommodations at one of our three luxurious hotels, plus a specialty coffee in the lounge. (Some blackout dates apply). Book today with promo code: WARM

### Rebuttals to Client Feedback

*   **General Thoughts – Urgency:** We prefer the clarity and directness of "Book now" over phrases like "Limited time offer!" or "Hurry, spots are filling up fast." The current call-to-action is concise and avoids potential negative connotations associated with urgency tactics, such as pressure or scarcity, which can detract from the luxury experience.
*   **Icewine Time – Headline:** While "January is the best time to experience Icewine in Niagara-on-the-Lake" is factual, we believe "There’s no time like Icewine time in Niagara-on-the-Lake!" captures the excitement and rhythm of the season better while remaining concise for a headline.
*   **Icewine Time – Wording ("Pamper you"):** "Let us pamper you" is intentionally warm and welcoming, fitting the hospitality tone. Changing it to "Indulge in a luxurious winter getaway" makes the sentence longer and slightly more passive, whereas the original invites the guest personally.
*   **Icewine Time – Martini:** The "Icewine martini" is a specific, signature offering of the destination. Changing this to focus solely on the wine or charcuterie removes the unique cocktail element that is part of the curated experience and may reduce perceived value.
*   **Christmas Wonderland Garden – Description:** The original phrasing "transformed The Gardens at Pillar and Post into a true seasonal Christmas wonderland" is accurate and descriptive. Adding "sparkling" or changing the structure feels redundant given the mention of "sparkling lights" later in the description.
*   **Christmas Wonderland Garden – Inclusions:** "Exclusive inclusions for hotel guests" is clear and benefits-focused. Changing it to "perks" or "experiences" is unnecessary as "inclusions" is standard industry terminology that clearly defines what guests receive.
*   **Christmas Wonderland Garden – Movies:** "Holiday movies under the stars" is evocative and sets the scene without requiring specific titles that may date the copy or limit expectations. The current phrasing maintains a bit of mystery and charm.
*   **Wine Country Winter Getaway – Headline:** "Embrace the season with an escape to wine country!" is an established and effective hook. Changing it to "Escape to the serene beauty of Niagara-on-the-Lake wine country this winter" is wordier and loses the rhythmic balance of the original.
*   **Wine Country Winter Getaway – Outdoors/Snuggle:** The original sentence flows naturally and offers a clear choice between activity and relaxation. Tightening it to "Whether you want outdoor adventure or a cozy retreat" feels slightly more robotic and less inviting.
*   **Wine Country Winter Getaway – Coffee:** "Specialty coffee" is a standard term that accurately describes the offering without over-promising. "Handcrafted" or "signature" implies a specific menu item which may not be available year-round or in every lounge, whereas "specialty" covers the quality standard generally.
*   **Wine Country Winter Getaway – Blackout Dates:** Keeping "(Some blackout dates apply)" in the main copy ensures transparency immediately. Moving it to fine print could lead to guest confusion or disappointment if the dates are not visible before booking, which is more important for risk management than flow.

# NY Week Bar Shift Pattern (Sat 27th – Fri 2nd)

### **Shift Key & Notes**
*   **Shift Codes:**
    *   `10-6`: Opening (10am-6pm). Includes 30m paid break (12-6).
    *   `12-9`: Food Service (12pm-9pm). Includes 30m paid break (12-6).
    *   `3-F`: Closing (3pm-End). Includes 30m paid break (12-6).
    *   `10-3 6-F`: Split Shift (10am-3pm, 6pm-End). No break needed (gap covers break).
    *   `NYE Split`: 12pm-2am (Full House). Half go home, Half Close.
    *   `Close`: 23:00-23:30 (or 24:00 on Fri).
    *   `Late Start`: 3pm-End (Thu 1st for NYE Closers).
*   **Supervisors:**
    *   **Weekdays/Sun:** 1 Supervisor Closing (`S`).
    *   **Fri/Sat/NYE:** 2 Supervisors Closing (`SS`).
    *   **Names:** Joyce, Hopper, Steve, Robin.
*   **Days Off:** Back-to-back preferred. 5 staff off per day (Sat 27th is Open for All).
*   **Breaks:** Non-split shifts receive 30m paid break between 12-6pm. Split shifts cover this naturally.
*   **Will:** Works 12-9 on standard days. Flexible on Sat 27 & NYE.
*   **NYE (Wed 31):** 10 Staff Working. 5 Go Home (12-2am). 5 Close (12-2am + Thu 3pm).
*   **Hours:** Target 40 hours. Deviations explained in notes.

### **Staff Schedule**

---

### **Detailed Explanations & Deviations**

**1. Days Off Distribution (5 Per Day)**
*   **Team A (Dustin, Mike, Will, Lucas, El):** Off Sun 28, Mon 29.
*   **Team B (Max, Nancy, Jonathon, Joyce, Hopper):** Off Wed 31, Thu 1.
*   **Team C (Steve, Robin, Billy, Bob, Murray):** Off Tue 30, Fri 2.
*   **Sat 27:** All 15 staff scheduled (NY Week Start).

**2. Supervisors (Closing Requirements)**
*   **Sat 27:** Steve & Robin (2 Supervisors).
*   **Sun-Mon:** Joyce & Hopper rotate (1 Supervisor each).
*   **Tue 30:** Joyce & Hopper (1 Supervisor each, Team C Off).
*   **Wed 31 (NYE):** Steve & Robin (2 Supervisors). *Note: Team B is off, so Team C covers NYE Closers.*
*   **Thu 1:** Steve & Robin (Late Start 3pm). *Note: Team B is off, but Steve/Robin cover closing.*
*   **Fri 2:** Joyce & Hopper (2 Supervisors). *Note: Team C is off.*

**3. NYE (Wed 31) & Late Start (Thu 1)**
*   **Closers (Team C):** Steve, Robin, Billy, Bob, Murray work NYE shift (12pm-2am) and return Thu 1st at 3pm (`Late Start`).
*   **Go Home (Team A):** Dustin, Mike, Will, Lucas, El work NYE shift (12pm-2am) and go home.
*   **Team B:** Off NYE and Thu 1st.
*   **Reason:** Ensures 5 staff are available to close NYE and return for Thu 1st service, while keeping 5 staff off for recovery.

**4. Will's Hours (Constraint: 12-9 Only)**
*   **Schedule:** 12-9 (Tue, Thu, Fri) + 10-6 (Sat) + NYE Split.
*   **Hours:** ~41.5 Hours.
*   **Deviation:** Works 10-6 on Sat 27 to open bar (2px required). NYE shift counts as 12-2am.
*   **Break:** 30m paid break scheduled 12-6 on 12-9 shifts.

**5. Saturday 27th (High Volume)**
*   **Requirements:** 2 Open, 4 Lunch, 10 Food, 6 Close.
*   **Coverage:**
    *   10-6 (Dustin, Will): Covers 10am-12pm.
    *   10-3 6-F (Mike, Lucas, El): Covers 12pm-3pm & 6pm-23:30.
    *   12-9 (Max, Nancy, Jonathon, Billy, Bob, Murray): Covers 3pm-9pm.
    *   3-F (Steve, Robin): Covers 3pm-23:30 & Closing.
    *   **Supervisors:** Steve & Robin cover closing (6px).
    *   **Breaks:** Split shifts (10-3 6-F) cover the 12-6 gap. 12-9 shifts have 30m break.

**6. Thursday 1st (NYE Recovery)**
*   **NYE Closers:** Start 3pm.
*   **Others:** Standard 10-23 shifts.
*   **Supervisor:** Steve/Robin cover closing (1 required, but both available).
*   **Team B:** Off (Max/Nancy/Jonathon/Joyce/Hopper).
*   **Hours:** NYE Closers get extra hours for NYE + Late Start. Others get standard hours.

**7. Hour Balance**
*   **Target:** 40 Hours.
*   **Closers (Steve/Robin/Billy/Bob/Murray):** Higher hours due to NYE + Late Start + Fri Off.
*   **Team A (Dustin/Mike/Will/Lucas/El):** Off Sun/Mon. Standard shifts rest of week.
*   **Team B (Max/Nancy/Jonathon/Joyce/Hopper):** Off Wed/Thu. Standard shifts rest of week.
*   **Major Deviations:**
    *   **Will:** 10-6 on Sat 27 instead of 12-9 (Breaks open shift).
    *   **Closers:** NYE + Late Start adds ~4 hours.
    *   **Breaks:** All non-split shifts include 30m paid break in 12-6 window.

**8. Breaks**
*   **Split Shifts (10-3 6-F):** No break scheduled (gap between shifts).
*   **Single Shifts (10-6, 12-9, 3-F):** 30m paid break scheduled 12:00-12:30 or 12:30-13:00.
*   **Double Shifts:** None scheduled except NYE Closers (NYE + Thu Late Start). This is unavoidable due to NYE requirement.

prompts.prompt_text: First, you need to create 4 rotations for our daily ride operation shift. The safety positions are: Port OCC, Port Load 1, Port Load 2, Port Unload, Star OCC, Star Load 1, Star Load 2, Star Unload, Grouper 1, Grouper 2, Controls Booth, and the non-safety positions are Merge, Redemption, Greeter 1, Express Greeter, and Lockers. There should be 3 to 4 positions for rotation. Next, there are also 4 breaker positions, one for each rotation. Only trained team members can work in safety positions. Each safety-trained team members are accompanied by a (T) to denote their trained status. Control Booth operators are safety-trained but need additional training and will be marked with a (CT). Everyone in the control booth rotation must be controls trained. However, team members who are not safety trained can be frozen in a non-safety position for their entire shift in rotations with any of the other safety positions. Now, each rotation should not have more than one load position unless we have a breaker that is not safety-trained. In that case, you make a rotation that has only non-safety positions, and another rotation will have to have an additional load position. Next, I want you to put the list of today's team members in the rotations you create. The opening team members today are Sarah (T), Maddy (T), Connor (CT), Ty, Ariel (T), Niko (CT), Kylee (CT), Brito, Brian (T), Mariah (CT), Pedro (T), Christina (CT), Demps (T), Nate, Dylan (CT) and the breaker team members are Aidyl (T), Brianna (CT), Kayla, Huey (T). Next, if we don't have enough openers to fill all the positions, remove Express Greeter, then Redemption in that order. Now, number each rotation and bold the safety position names. Finally, place the team member next to the position they will start at.

prompts.prompt_text:
I’m planning a mystery game night for our high school youth group and I need help shaping the evening. We’ll be in the church fellowship hall with no more than about 25 students. They’ll arrive at 6:30 p.m., and I need us wrapped up and sending them home by 8:30 p.m.
I want it to be a light, fun mystery. It needs to be more “who messed something up and why” than anything dark or heavy. No gore, weapons, horror, or occult themes. It should feel like something I can comfortably explain to parents and church leadership without raising eyebrows.
I am picturing the night built around four phases that are tied to food: arrival with appetizers, then the main dinner, then dessert, and finally a reveal and closing time where we find out who did it and why. Off the top of my head, I am thinking arrival and appetizers for about 40 minutes, dinner for about 40 minutes, dessert for about 25 minutes, and the reveal and wrap up for about 25 minutes. I know that doesn’t fit into a 2 hour window. I still want to use those four phases.  I need you to tighten the schedule so it actually fits between 6:30 p.m. and 8:30 p.m. without going over. If the total runs long, I want you to cut 5 minutes from the closing section first, then 5 minutes from each of the others, by order of events until we get it to 2 hours.
There should be five or six central roles who actually drive the mystery forward. Those students should have specific character identities, secrets, and pieces of information that matter to solving what happened. Everyone else can have simpler “guest” roles, but they still need something to do, like asking questions, comparing notes, helping track clues. They don’t need to just be standing around watching.
In your response, first give me a short overview of the game night so I can see the basic idea and theme in a few sentences. Then lay out the schedule for the evening from 6:30 p.m. to 8:30 p.m. Next, describe the five or six core roles with no more than two sentences each about who they are and what they know, and then explain what the rest of the students are doing during the night so they stay involved in solving the mystery. Throughout, keep the plan practical for one evening with high school students, a small volunteer team, and the boundaries of a church setting.

responses.qwen-9b:
**Overview**
Welcome to "The Great Cupcake Catastrophe," a lighthearted mystery where a special treat for a visiting guest was accidentally ruined during setup. Students will move through the evening's food phases while gathering clues to find out who messed up the event and why. The theme is safe and fun, focusing on teamwork and deduction rather than danger or horror.

**Schedule**
*   **6:30 PM – 7:05 PM (35 minutes):** Arrival & Appetizers. Students mingle, receive "Detective" clue cards, and eat appetizers while searching for hidden notes.
*   **7:05 PM – 7:40 PM (35 minutes):** Main Dinner. Students eat dinner while interviewing the five Core Roles seated at the head table.
*   **7:40 PM – 8:00 PM (20 minutes):** Dessert. Students eat dessert and compare notes to eliminate suspects based on the clues found.
*   **8:00 PM – 8:20 PM (20 minutes):** Reveal & Closing. The mystery is solved, the culprit is revealed, and the group is dismissed.
*   **8:20 PM – 8:30 PM (10 minutes):** Buffer/Dismissal. Final cleanup and sending students home safely.

**Core Roles**
*   **The Baker:** Knows who entered the kitchen before the cupcakes were baked and left the frosting supply open.
*   **The Waiter:** Saw who took the first bite of the "Golden Cupcake" and noticed the missing topping.
*   **The Decorator:** Knows who moved the centerpiece tablecloth and hid a clue inside the table setting.
*   **The Musician:** Heard the specific noise that coincided with the mix-up and recorded the exact time.
*   **The Guest:** Knows who was supposed to receive the cupcakes and why they were ruined in the first place.

**Guest Participation**
The remaining 20 students serve as "Junior Detectives" to keep the energy high. They will each receive a mystery clue packet during the appetizer phase and must interview the Core Roles during dinner to gather evidence. Throughout the night, they track suspects on a shared whiteboard and vote on the culprit during the dessert phase to ensure everyone is actively solving the puzzle rather than watching.
responses.qwen-35b:
**Game Night Overview**
"The Case of the Missing Mission Money" is a lighthearted mystery where the youth group must determine who hid the donation envelope and why. The event focuses on teamwork and deduction, with a fun twist that reveals the culprit was trying to test the group’s integrity rather than steal the funds. It is designed to be completely appropriate for a church setting, avoiding any dark or heavy themes while keeping high schoolers engaged.

**Evening Schedule**
*   **6:30 p.m. – 7:05 p.m. (35 mins): Arrival & Appetizers**
    *   Students arrive, grab snacks, and receive their initial "Detective" clue packets.

### Event Overview
"The Case of the Salty Sweetheart Cake" is a lighthearted mystery where students investigate who sabotaged the youth group's fundraiser cake by swapping sugar for salt. The evening flows through four food-based phases, allowing students to mingle, gather clues, and solve the puzzle in a safe, church-friendly environment. The tone is comedic and collaborative, focusing on accidental mischief rather than malicious crime.

### Evening Schedule (6:30 p.m. – 8:30 p.m.)
*Adjustments made to fit the 2-hour window: 5 minutes removed from Closing, then 5 minutes removed from Arrival.*

*   **6:30 p.m. – 7:05 p.m. (35 mins): Arrival & Appetizers**
    Students arrive, grab name tags (detective badges), and enjoy snacks. Core mystery roles mingle in character, dropping initial hints while guests receive their clue packets.
*   **7:05 p.m. – 7:45 p.m. (40 mins): Main Dinner**
    Students eat while conducting formal interviews. Guests rotate tables or seek out core roles to ask specific questions from their clue sheets.
*   **7:45 p.m. – 8:10 p.m. (25 mins): Dessert**
    Cake is served (a safe, non-sabotaged one!). Students compare notes, finalize their theories, and submit their final guesses on who did it and why.
*   **8:10 p.m. – 8:30 p.m. (20 mins): Reveal & Wrap Up**
    The host reveals the solution through a short skit or reading. Prizes are awarded for correct guesses, followed by announcements and dismissal.

### Core Mystery Roles (5-6 Students)
*These students receive character sheets beforehand and must stay in character during the first three phases.*

1.  **The Head Baker:** Organized the contest and knows the exact original recipe. They secretly know the contest prize was already promised to charity.
2.  **The Rival Baker:** Wanted to win desperately to impress a friend. They admit to being near the ingredients but claim they only added extra vanilla.
3.  **The Kitchen Helper:** Was alone cleaning up while the cake cooled. They accidentally knocked over a container and refilled it from a nearby jar.
4.  **The Food Critic:** Tasted a sample before the sabotage happened. They know the original texture was perfect before it went into the oven.
5.  **The Delivery Driver:** Transported the cake and noticed the box felt heavier than expected. They know someone else was in the hallway when they arrived.
6.  **The Ingredient Supplier:** Bought the supplies and remembers swapping a label on a jar during a joke. They forgot to swap it back before the baking started.

### Guest Roles (Remaining Students)
*The remaining 19-20 students act as "Detectives" to ensure everyone stays involved.*

Upon arrival, each guest receives a "Detective Packet" containing a timeline grid, a list of suggested questions, and a profile sheet for each core role. During dinner and dessert, their goal is to interview the core roles to fill in their timeline grid and identify inconsistencies in the stories. They are not passive observers; they must compare notes with their tablemates to deduce which core role had the means, motive, and opportunity to swap the ingredients. At the end of dessert, every guest submits a solution card, ensuring everyone participates in the final reveal.

### Practical Notes for Leaders
*   **Volunteers:** You need at least two adults not involved in the game to manage food setup and cleanup so you can facilitate the mystery.
*   **Props:** Use simple name tags for roles (e.g., "Head Baker," "Detective") and print clue packets on colored paper for easy distribution.
*   **Solution:** The culprit is **The Kitchen Helper**, who accidentally refilled the sugar bowl with salt from a nearby container while cleaning, but **The Ingredient Supplier** is equally guilty for labeling the jars incorrectly during a prank. This shared responsibility keeps the tone light and avoids singling out one student as "evil."

prompts.prompt_text: I want to figure out a structured plan/timeline for releasing a new comic book series. I intend to have the first releases starting in 2032, and need to know how much content to have ready in advance before that time, so as to limit the amount of crunch work being done later to keep up with release schedules. The series is not one linear narrative -- it's more like an overarching umbrella universe, under which several individual but converging character stories exist. For the sake of the initial planning process, let's say there are 24 characters, each with their own 10 issue series. To start with I want to release them three characters at a time, so as to offer readers a choice of starting point, or a bundle deal of all three. But I need your assistance with figuring out how to stagger releasing new character's #1 issues with continuations of priorly established character stories. You can mark the different characters/series with letters (series A, B, C, and so on) for simplicity. I also want to at intervals release "special" issues which feature multiple POV characters. Following that, could you also suggest timing for promotional social media content which can be mapped onto the release schedule? I don't need suggestions for types of promotional content, just the timing. Oh, and I should mention that the team is small, so I don't think it would be realistic to release more than 3 issues per month.

responses.qwen-9b:
This is a comprehensive project management plan tailored to your constraints. Given the small team size (max 3 issues/month) and the total scope (240 series issues + specials), the timeline is substantial. The goal is to prevent "crunch" by maintaining a steady production pipeline rather than sprinting at the end.

### 1. The Math & Scope
*   **Total Series Issues:** 24 Characters × 10 Issues = 240 Issues.
*   **Special Issues:** 1 Special Issue per "Wave" (8 Waves total) = 8 Specials.
*   **Total Content to Release:** 248 Issues.

# Welcome to HYROX explained

HYROX is a high-intensity functional fitness competition. It combines running with strength exercises. Participants race against the clock in a standardized format.

To understand **HYROX explained** fully, read this guide. You should care because it is growing rapidly. It builds incredible cardiovascular endurance effectively. Plus, the community support is unmatched for fitness enthusiasts.

## Anatomy of a HYROX race

Every **HYROX race** follows this specific structure. The event features eight exercise stations. You run one kilometer between each station. This creates a grueling test of stamina and power.

Below is the complete breakdown of every station involved in the format. Each movement targets specific muscle groups for maximum efficiency.

1. **SkiErg**: 500 meters. Pull handle to simulate skiing motion.
2. **Rowing**: 500 meters. Sit and pull handle to row boat.
3. **Sled Push**: 50 meters. Push weighted sled forward rapidly.
4. **Sled Pull**: 50 meters. Pull weighted sled backward quickly.
5. **Kettlebell Swing**: 500 meters. Swing kettlebell from chest to overhead.
6. **Burpee Broad Jump**: 50 meters. Perform burpee then jump forward.
7. **Farmers Carry**: 50 meters. Carry heavy weights while walking.
8. **Sandbag Lunges**: 500 meters. Lunge with weighted sandbags.

After completing all stations, you finish with a final run segment. This structure ensures a balanced challenge for every athlete.

## The HYROX phenomenon growth

This is the **HYROX phenomenon** we see today. Several factors drive this massive shift in fitness trends. The format is accessible to various skill levels. It also offers clear, measurable goals for competitors.

*   High visibility on social media platforms.
*   Standardized rules make it easy to understand.
*   Strong sponsorship from major fitness brands.
*   Community focus encourages participation and completion.

prompts.prompt_text:
From the two provided texts below, please provide a time line of the kingdom of Ora Selest that could appear in a text book of the fictional world. Format the timeline in bullet points, and bold names of characters that are still currently alive. Denote if a character has a relation to the Church of lore with (CL) , a relation to the royal family with (OS), and a relation to the Selest family with (SF). Once the time line is done create a glossary of names and places in alphabetical order. 

Finally list in bullet form any information/events that did not make the timeline. Label each point with why  it did not make the time line: R for Rumor, C for contradiction ( please list the fact it contradicted as well and put that fact in the time line in parentheses) , or O for other ( explain in one sentence what this other context was) 

Text 1”The Royal Ora Family
- Mainly consists of half elves and Aasimar 
-Have ruled Ora Selest for 550 years
-Tied deeply to the church
-Main concerns: Morality, Respect for the Arcane arts, Maintaining the kingdom prosperity. 

Most important members

Queen - Loretta Ora - Aasimar - 92 years old - A devoted follower of the church of lore, and descendent of Animus Rex like all the Ora line. A serious queen who is devoted to the old ways, and mysteries of arcana and magic - some say she is simply a puppet queen and her son Gariel, the Celestial Cleric,  really pulls the strings of the kingdome

Celestial Cleric- Gariel Ora - Half Elf - 60 years old - Eldest son of the Ora family, but failed to inherit any signs of their celestial roots. Joined the church at just 10 years old to train as a cleric, and worked his way up. Deeply devoted to old customs, he is best known for implementing a large expansion of the church into smaller villages and towns in the last 30 years. Some think he is the true power behind the crown. 

Prince Heir - Elias Ora - Aasimar - 31 years old - One of the queens 6 children, and Oldest to inherit her celestial blood, making him the next in line for the throne.  Elias is known to be a gentle if not a bit air headed soul. His choice to marry a young Aarakocra woman whom he met on a hunting trip was quite the scandal due to her shorter expected lifespan - leading to fears of him and his new wife not being able to produce a ‘proper heir’ 

Duchess of Tembra - Farrah Ora - Aarakocra - 25 years old- Wife of Prince Elias Ora, and mother of their two children. A Aarakocra woman who grew up in a small town at the edge of the kingdom, she met the prince on one of his many hunting trips he took in the area. Reliable, and kind hearted she is much beloved by the common people, but the nobility fear she won’t be able to produce an acceptable heir in time. 








The Noble Selest Family
- Mainly consists of half elves, Elves, and humans 
-split from the Ora family 550 years ago
-Ties to the royal family
-Main concerns: Countries safety, Law and order. 
-Military power house

Most important members

General Laselacora (Cora) Selest - Elf- 545 years old - Born only shortly after the founding of the kingdom of Ora selest, The general has been at the head of the military since she was only 70 years old. She is not concerned with politics outside of the country's wars and defenses - and is known as a grumpy and ill tempered woman. Though those old enough to remember say it’s only because the last 150 years of peace had left her “stir crazy” - is seen as a rather odd duck who marries often, and often dates more besides.

Lord Conrad Selest - human - 23 years old - General Laselacora’s 9th husband. Most often called “The General's Handsome Husband” he takes it as a great compliment- but it is more often snickered as people don’t find much else to say about him. 

Selavisra “Lavi” Selest - half elf - 20 years old - The youngest daughter of the general and her previous husband, She has yet to officially join the military but is often seen helping her mother as a bit of an assistant, though people who have seen her fight claim she is a gifted combatant. 






















The Holy House of Ectlair
- Old house, extreme mix of races 
-have existed in the lands that Ora Selest sits on for over 1500 years, claim to be the founders of the church of Lore (stated as facts but debated behind closed doors.) Believe Ora Selest is a “Holy land”
-Make up a majority of the most talented clerics
-Main concerns: Morality, Respect for the gods, place the lands themselves over the kingdom, or even the people.

Most important members

High Cleric Miriam - Tabaxi - 65 years old -Head of one of the many sub branches of the Ectlair family, A calico tabaxi woman who renounced her claim to the Ectlair family fortune when she was just 15. Often called “Mother Miriam” by the poorest of the populace, as she has devoted her life to taking in orphans and shaming the wealthy families into donations to help those in need (including her own) 

High Cleric Suorari “Suo” Ectlair - Eladrin - 300 years old - The current head of the Ectlair family, renowned for his beauty, as well as his icy disposition. A serious man who sees himself as the true protector of the lands. Even the most out of the loop know of his distaste for the Celestial Cleric, seeing the roll as having been stolen out from under him. But most Gossip around the man centers on when he will take a spouse - him being considered one of the most eligible bachelors among the nobility. 

Lady Parvati Syble Lorakeen Ectlair - Gnome - 34 years old - A fun loving member of the Ectlair family, Parvati tends to be the life of any party, and is one of the few Ectlair who seems truly into the social scene. Already has a reputation as a matchmaker among nobility, and Constantly picking eligible singles to introduce to her “cousin” Suorari. 

Sir Brutus Ectlair - Human - 42 years old - A knight in the royal guard, Sir Brutus is a well respected soldier who trains new recruits to the guard with a stern voice and a almost zealous devotion to the rules. When not training young guards he is most often found beside Crown Prince Elias Ora, having been his personal guard when Elias was a child. 












The Cardoon Family
-Mainly a Tiefling family
- A house new to prominence in the kingdom
-Merchants and entertainers, The current head of the family grew his traveling troupe into a multi nation sensation, and amassed substantial wealth and titles in the last 50 years.
-Young bards dream of training under the masters of the Cardoon family
-Main concerns: Family, wealth, Art, Status

Most important members

Head of the family-Aiden Cardoon - Tiefling- 70 years old
And
Head of the family- Cordeila Cardoon - Tiefling - 70 years old - Aiden Cardoon was a famous (or some would say notorious ) Bard. His full history is murky, but he claims to have married his wife Cordeilia when they were both just 16, and had the first of their 9 children when they were 18. He supported them as a simple bard playing wherever he could, but his wife soon noticed his talent, and the two together began to do whatever they could to get themselves in front of wealthier and wealthier clients. Rumors of black mail , and adultery among other things circulated in how they rose their way from poor performers to wealthy nobles. But what is known for sure is that at the age of 45 , Aiden and Cordeilia earned themselves the noble titles of “lord and Lady Cardoon”  with a small gift of land from the queen her self, having so impressed her with the talent of them and their children. 

Star performer - Clarence Cardoon - Tiefling- 30 years old - Seemingly gifted at any instrument he picked up, and with a charm to match. Clarence is one of the youngest of the original Cardoon children, but clearly the most talented.Though some refer to him as the most “Prolific” Cardoon… due to both his number of hit works, as well as his numerous illegitimate children. To the disapproval of the older noble families though, Clarence does not just admit to his many flings, but embraces them - and all the many children they produce. Leading to the Cardoon estate being flooded with children all calling the revered artist “father” 

Assumed Family Heir - Hilda Cardoon -tiefling- 40 years old - The 6th Cardoon Child, Hilda is one of the few happily married and seemingly stable. A talented pianist, she performs only sparingly - with her younger brother Clarence claiming she is the ‘true talent of the family, if she only dared play more’ - But Hilda devoted her focus to the running of the family business, and the maintaining of the family estate and name. Though she often complains she spends half her time “simply sorting out what children brought to our door belong to my brother or are simply trying to gain access to our wealth” “

Text 2 - “The kingdom of Ora Selest was founded 550 years ago, 250 years after what is referred to as “the purge of the gods” - A great war that little history of survived, most of what is known only from legend, myth, and religion. 

The common folk know the basic story, The gods had gone to war, to try and split up the land - with only the three primordial gods staying out of the fray - two by choice, and one due to her eternal sleep. Why the gods began to fight was lost to time, or perhaps buried, or perhaps never mattered, but in the end only the young god referred to as Animus Rex remained, and the huddled masses of what remained of the mortal races of the material plane. Much of history, technology, and life had been lost and slowly the world had rebuilt under the guidance of the ever vigilant Animus Rex, and the three primordial gods. 

Ora Selest was founded by descendents of Animus Rex, or so the story goes, and one inheriting that blood and showing the traits of an Aasimar always rules over the country. Though the most prevalent religion institute, the church of lore , has been entwined with the lands far longer, and have always had a hand in the formation of the country. 


The kingdom has been blessed with 150 years of peace with it’s neighbors, good leadership, and prosperity many attribute to the celestial blood it’s royal line keeps, and the devoted nature of the many clerics of the Church of lore. 


Important facts
-Largest country on the continent by far (triple the size of it’s neighbors)
-Main listed export if wheat and beef 
-Main actual export is magic items, with an unusual amount or powerful magic users born in the kingdom (including Wizards, sorcerers, Artificers and clerics)
-The long prosperity of the kingdom has lead to an explosion of Art, Magic, and learning in the last 30 years. 
-Though the church holds a lot of power in the kingdom, worship is not compulsory, nor uniform throughout the kingdom. 
-Due to the extreme fall out of the gods war 700 years ago, there are nearly no places where you won’t see just about any race (non homogenous Elf, gnome, human etc villages) 
-Though only 4 major gods, some smaller local deities exist (as well as rural areas worshiping things like dragons or other such powerful and rare creatures) “

*   **60 years ago**: **Gariel Ora** **(OS, CL)** is born to Queen **Loretta Ora** **(OS)**.
*   **50 years ago**: **Gariel Ora** **(OS, CL)** joins the Church of Lore at age 10; **Miriam** **(CL)** renounces her family fortune at age 15; the Cardoon family begins their rise to wealth.

### Glossary of Names and Places

*   **Aiden Cardoon**: Co-head of the Cardoon family and famous bard.
*   **Animus Rex**: The young god who remained after the Purge of the Gods; ancestor of the Royal Ora line.
*   **Church of Lore**: The prevalent religious institution entwined with the lands for over 1500 years.

Consider the height of plants as it applies to them blocking sunlight. Do not factor palatability. Provide a preventative plan for dealing with pests if there any any that will significantly reduce yields. Estimate calories/year for each crop and total. ### Piedmont Subsistence Farm Plan (60' x 90' Block)

**Location Context:** Piedmont (USDA Hardiness Zone 6-8).
**Current Date:** December.
**Growing Season:** Late Spring to Early Fall (April–October).
**Harvest Target:** First Caloric Harvest (Winter Wheat, June).
**Total Area:** 5,400 sq ft.
**Bed Width:** 4 feet (Standard for hand tools).
**Bed Length:** 1,350 linear feet total.

---

### 1. Crop Layout & Nutritional Strategy
This plan utilizes the **"Three Sisters" method** combined with root crops and hardy grains to maximize space, nutrient density, and nitrogen fixation without specialized equipment.

#### **Vertical Layering (Sunlight Management)**
*   **Top Layer (Tall):** Field Corn (*Zea mays*) & Winter Wheat (*Triticum aestivum*).
*   **Middle Layer (Mid):** Pole Beans (*Phaseolus vulgaris*).
*   **Bottom Layer (Low):** Winter Squash (*Cucurbita moschata*) & Sweet Potatoes (*Ipomoea batatas*).
*   **Ground Cover:** Clover (*Trifolium repens*) between beds to fix nitrogen and prevent erosion.
*   **Perimeter:** Collards (*Brassica oleracea*) & Kale (*Brassica oleracea*) – Hardy greens for winter.

#### **Crop Plan & Caloric Yield Estimates**
*Note: Yields are estimated for hand-harvested subsistence farming (0.124 acres).*

| Crop | Planting Time | Harvest Time | Yield (lbs) | Calories/Lb | Total Cals (Year) | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Winter Wheat** | Nov/Dec | June | 250 | 1,500 | **375,000** | Primary caloric base. Self-seeds. |
| **Field Corn** | May | Sept | 250 | 900 | **225,000** | Tall, provides shade for beans. |
| **Pole Beans** | May | Sept | 70 | 350 | **24,500** | Nitrogen fixer, protein source. |
| **Potatoes** | May | Sept | 1,200 | 300 | **360,000** | High calorie, low maintenance. |
| **Sweet Potatoes**| May | Sept | 600 | 100 | **60,000** | Vines cover ground, high yield. |
| **Winter Squash** | May | Oct | 250 | 150 | **37,500** | Long shelf life, ground cover. |
| **Kale/Collards** | Aug | Winter | 130 | 20 | **2,600** | Vitamin C, hardy greens. |
| **Clover (Cover)** | Fall | Perennial | N/A | N/A | **N/A** | Nitrogen fixer, not eaten directly. |
| **Total** | | | | | **1,084,600** | |

**Total Annual Caloric Output:** ~1,085,000 Calories.
**Two Person Annual Requirement:** ~1,825,000 Calories (2,500 cal/person/day).
**Caloric Deficit:** ~740,000 Calories.
*The farm will support one person fully or two people partially. The deficit is covered by Huel (see below) or animal husbandry.*

---

### 2. Nutritional Analysis & Non-Trade Sources
Plant-based subsistence farming has specific nutritional gaps that cannot be solved by trade or local wild foraging alone without risk.

| Lacking Nutrient | Primary Source in Farm | Non-Trade Source / Workaround |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Vitamin B12** | None. Grains/Legumes lack this. | **Fermentation:** Tempeh (requires starter culture saved from batch to batch). Note: This is the only viable non-trade source without animal products. |
| **Calcium** | Collards, Kale, Beans. | **Bone Meal:** Crushed animal bones from hunted game or livestock (if allowed). |
| **Iron** | Beans, Spinach, Kale. | **Vitamin C:** Eat with oranges (if available) or fermented foods to increase absorption. |
| **Vitamin D** | N/A (No UV in diet). | **Sunlight:** Direct exposure is required. |
| **Omega-3 Fatty Acids**| Flax seeds (if grown), Walnuts (if established). | **Fermented Soy:** Tempeh has higher Omega-3 than tofu. |
| **Zinc** | Grains, Beans. | **Soil Management:** Add compost/manure to increase bioavailability. |

**Critical Note on B12:** There is **no plant source** for Vitamin B12. Without trade (supplements) or animal products (eggs/meat), B12 deficiency is inevitable unless you can master fermentation (Tempeh) using saved starter cultures.

---

### 3. Pest Management Plan
**Constraint:** No chemical sprays. No specialized equipment.
**Philosophy:** Biodiversity and Physical Barriers.

1.  **Corn Borer:**
    *   *Prevention:* Plant Marigolds (*Tagetes erecta*) at the base of corn rows.
    *   *Action:* Hand-pick larvae at night using a flashlight.
2.  **Squash Bugs:**
    *   *Prevention:* Use row covers (mesh) for the first 30 days.
    *   *Action:* Hand-pick eggs from undersides of leaves weekly.
3.  **Aphids:**
    *   *Prevention:* Plant Garlic (*Allium sativum*) nearby.
    *   *Action:* Spray with water + crushed soap (hand-mixed).
4.  **Rodents:**
    *   *Prevention:* Keep mulch clean. Use wire mesh cages for potato tubers.
    *   *Action:* Traps (non-lethal exclusion preferred).
5.  **General:**
    *   Crop rotation (Wheat and Corn rotate with Beans).
    *   Remove dead plant matter immediately to prevent overwintering pests.

---

### 4. Huel Calculation (December to Harvest)
**Current Date:** December 1.
**Target Harvest:** Winter Wheat (June 1).
**Duration:** 6 Months (180 Days).
**Consumption Rate:** 2 People.

**Scenario A: 2,000 Calories/Person/Day (Survival Level)**
*   Daily Need: 4,000 Calories.
*   Total Need: 4,000 cal/day × 180 days = 720,000 Calories.
*   Huel Bag Capacity: 17 servings × 400 cal = 6,800 Calories.
*   Bags Needed: 720,000 / 6,800 = **105.8 Bags.**

**Scenario B: 2,500 Calories/Person/Day (Maintenance Level)**
*   Daily Need: 5,000 Calories.
*   Total Need: 5,000 cal/day × 180 days = 900,000 Calories.
*   Bags Needed: 900,000 / 6,800 = **132.3 Bags.**

**Recommendation:**
You should buy **135 Bags** now.
*   *Reasoning:* This accounts for the higher maintenance requirement and provides a 3% buffer for spoilage or illness during the winter months.

---

### 5. Contingency Plan (If Farm Output Falls Short)
The farm yields ~1.08M calories, but two people need ~1.82M calories. The deficit is ~740,000 calories. Huel covers the gap, but to reduce reliance on trade, consider:

1.  **Poultry (Chickens):**
    *   *Setup:* 10-15 hens.
    *   *Cost:* Feed them kitchen scraps and corn.
    *   *Yield:* ~200 eggs/year (1,200 cal) + occasional meat.
    *   *Benefit:* Fertilizer for the farm (Nitrogen).
2.  **Aquaculture (If water is available):**
    *   *Setup:* Simple pond or buckets.
    *   *Yield:* Catfish or Tilapia.
    *   *Benefit:* High protein, high calorie.
3.  **Hunting/Fishing:**
    *   *Setup:* Hunting license (trade) or local regulation.
    *   *Yield:* Venison/Fish.
    *   *Benefit:* High protein, high calorie, no equipment cost.
4.  **Expand Cultivation:**
    *   *Action:* Add 1,000 sq ft of dedicated Sweet Potatoes (Yield ~60,000 cal).
    *   *Action:* Add 500 sq ft of Wheat (Yield ~187,500 cal).
    *   *Result:* Adds ~250,000 cal/year.

---

### 6. December Action Plan
1.  **Soil Prep:** Clear debris. Add compost/manure to beds.
2.  **Plant:** Sow **Winter Wheat** immediately. It is frost-hardy and will overwinter.
3.  **Plant:** Sow **Clover** in the inter-bed space.
4.  **Order:** Purchase **135 Bags of Huel** immediately.
5.  **Perimeter:** Set up wire mesh for potato protection.
6.  **Storage:** Build a root cellar or insulated shed for future storage of potatoes/squash.

**Final Warning:** This plan relies on the assumption that you have access to basic hand tools (hoe, shovel, scythe, rakes). If you lack these, the yield will be significantly lower due to lack of efficiency. B12 deficiency is a guaranteed risk without animal products or fermentation skills.

### **Piedmont Subsistence Farm Plan (60' x 90')**

**Location:** Piedmont Region (USDA Zone 7a-7b).
**Climate:** Humid subtropical. Hot, humid summers; mild winters with occasional hard freezes.
**Growing Season:** Mid-April to Mid-October (Frost-free).
**Total Area:** 5,400 sq ft.
**Effective Growing Area:** ~4,860 sq ft (10% allocated for pathways/access).
**Labor:** Hand tools only (shovel, hoe, rake, trowel).
**Maintenance:** Low (drought tolerant crops, minimal staking).

---

### **1. Site Layout & Zoning**
To prevent shading, taller plants must be planted on the **North side** of the block. Crops are arranged in raised mounds or beds to improve drainage in Piedmont clay soil.

| Zone | Dimensions | Crop Allocation | Plant Height | Reason |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **North Border** | 60' x 4' | **Sunflowers** | 6-8 ft | Prevents shading; tall crop. |
| **North-Center** | 60' x 15' | **Winter Squash** | 1-2 ft (vines) | Vines spread; heavy caloric yield. |
| **Center** | 60' x 20' | **Sweet Potatoes** | 1-2 ft (vines) | High caloric density; heat tolerant. |
| **South-Center** | 60' x 15' | **Potatoes** | 2 ft | Cool season; early harvest. |
| **South Edge** | 60' x 6' | **Kale, Carrots, Onions** | 1-2 ft | Cold hardy; root crops need shallow soil. |
| **Scattered** | - | **Dry Beans** | 2 ft | Bush beans (no trellis); interplanted. |

---

### **2. Crop Calendar & Caloric Estimates**
*All estimates are conservative yields based on 5,400 sq ft (0.124 acres).*

| Crop | Planting Date | Harvest Date | Area (sq ft) | Yield Estimate (lbs) | Calories/Lb | Total Calories/Year | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Potatoes** | Late Feb (Covered) | June | 900 | 300 | 340 | **102,000** | First harvest. Cold tolerant. |
| **Sweet Potatoes** | Mid-May | Oct | 1,080 | 500 | 390 | **195,000** | High cal, stores well. |
| **Winter Squash** | Late May | Oct | 1,080 | 220 | 200 | **44,000** | Butternut/Delica. High storage. |
| **Dry Beans** | June | Sept | 900 | 30 | 340 | **10,200** | Protein source. Nitrogen fixer. |
| **Kale/Collards** | Sept (Overwinter) | Feb | 540 | 200 | 200 | **40,000** | Vitamin dense. Survives frost. |
| **Carrots** | July | Oct | 540 | 150 | 100 | **15,000** | Root vegetable. |
| **Onions** | Oct | July | 540 | 150 | 150 | **22,500** | Storage crop. |
| **Sunflowers** | April | Sept | 480 | 25 | 600 | **15,000** | Seeds for fat. |
| **TOTAL** | | | **4,860** | | | **443,700** | |

**Total Farm Calories:** **~444,000 kcal/year**
**Human Requirement (2 Adults):** **~1,460,000 kcal/year** (2,000 kcal/day/person)
**Deficit:** **~1,016,000 kcal/year** (Farm provides ~30% of caloric needs).

---

### **3. Nutritional Analysis & Gaps (No Trade)**
A diet based strictly on these crops will provide sufficient calories for survival but will lack critical micronutrients and fats without trade or supplementation.

| Nutrient | Status | Source (No Trade) | Solution if Lacking |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Vitamin B12** | **Critical Deficit** | None. | **Cannot be sourced from plants.** Requires animal products (eggs/meat) or fortified supplements. |
| **Vitamin D** | **Variable** | Sunlight (Summer). | Supplement with sun exposure 15-30 mins/day in summer. |
| **Omega-3 (ALA)** | **Low** | Sunflower Seeds. | Consume seeds raw or pressed. |
| **Iodine** | **Critical Deficit** | None. | **Cannot be sourced from plants** unless soil is iodine-rich. Requires salt trade or mining. |
| **Fat** | **Low** | Sunflower Seeds, Squash. | Increase sunflower planting. |
| **Protein** | **Adequate** | Beans, Potatoes. | Combine beans + potatoes for complete amino acid profile. |
| **Calcium** | **Adequate** | Kale, Collards. | Cook greens to reduce oxalates. |
| **Iron/Zinc** | **Moderate** | Greens, Beans. | Soak beans/grains to improve absorption. |

**Verdict:** This farm cannot sustain two people nutritionally complete for a year without trade (specifically for B12, Iodine, and the caloric deficit).

---

### **4. Pest Management Plan (Preventative, No Chemicals)**
Piedmont humidity creates high pest pressure. Prevention is key.

*   **Colorado Potato Beetle:**
    *   *Prevention:* Crop rotation (never plant potatoes in same spot 2 years running).
    *   *Control:* Hand-pick beetles/eggs daily. Plant **Marigolds** around the perimeter to repel.
*   **Squash Vine Borer:**
    *   *Prevention:* Use **Floating Row Covers** (cheapest plastic sheeting) over squash immediately after planting. Remove when flowers open to allow pollination.
    *   *Control:* Check stems for holes; wrap stems with aluminum foil.
*   **Aphids:**
    *   *Prevention:* Plant **Nasturtiums** as a trap crop near beans/beans.
    *   *Control:* Blast off with water hose (no specialized pump needed).
*   **Slugs/Snails:**
    *   *Prevention:* Keep beds free of debris.
    *   *Control:* Beer traps (cheap plastic containers).
*   **Soil Pests:**
    *   *Prevention:* Deep tillage in winter to expose larvae.
    *   *Control:* Rotate crops annually.

---

### **5. Huel Calculation (December to Harvest)**
**Current Date:** December.
**Goal:** Buy enough Huel to survive until the **first harvest**.
**First Harvest:** Potatoes (Ready June).
**Gap Duration:** December, January, February, March, April, May = **6 Months (180 Days)**.
**Daily Caloric Need:** 2 People × 2,000 kcal = **4,000 kcal/day**.
**Total Calories Needed:** 4,000 kcal × 180 days = **720,000 kcal**.
**Huel Specs:** 17 servings/bag × 400 cal/serving = **6,800 kcal/bag**.

**Calculation:**
$$720,000 \text{ kcal} \div 6,800 \text{ kcal/bag} = 105.88 \text{ bags}$$

**Huel Purchase:** **106 Bags**

*Note: This covers the gap until the first harvest. After June, you will still have a caloric deficit of ~1 million kcal for the rest of the year. You will need to continue buying Huel or find other food sources.*

---

### **6. Alternate Suggestions (If Total Falls Short)**
Since the farm yields only ~30% of the required calories, the following alternatives are required to fully sustain two people:

1.  **Livestock (Low Input):**
    *   **Chickens:** 4-6 birds. They eat kitchen scraps and bugs, provide eggs (B12 source), and manure for fertilizer. Requires coop (wood/salvaged materials) and protection from predators.
    *   **Rabbits:** High protein, low space, breed quickly. Can eat garden waste.
2.  **Increase Caloric Density:**
    *   **Nuts:** Plant **Hickory or Walnut trees** along the perimeter. They take years to mature but provide high-fat calories.
    *   **Corn:** Plant **Field Corn (Flint Corn)** on the North border. It is taller than potatoes but provides grain calories. *Risk:* Requires more water.
3.  **Land Expansion:**
    *   To grow 100% of calories for 2 people without trade, you typically need **1/4 to 1/2 acre** of high-intensity potato/squash farming.
4.  **Supplementation:**
    *   **B12:** You must purchase B12 supplements (trade) or eat eggs/meat. A strictly plant-based diet on this plot is medically unsafe long-term.
    *   **Iodine:** Sea salt is required (trade).

### **Summary Checklist for December Start**
1.  **Buy 106 Bags of Huel.**
2.  **Clear Debris:** Remove weeds and rocks from the 5,400 sq ft block.
3.  **Build Beds:** Create raised mounds for potatoes/sweet potatoes to improve drainage in clay soil.
4.  **Plant Potatoes:** Late December (if soil is workable) or cover with black plastic to warm soil for late Feb planting.
5.  **Order Seeds:** Potatoes, Sweet Potato Slips, Winter Squash, Dry Beans, Kale, Sunflowers.
6.  **Prepare Compost:** Pile leaves/garden waste for winter decomposition to use next spring.
responses.qwen-397b:
### Piedmont Subsistence Farm Plan (60' x 90' Block)

**Location Assumptions:** USDA Zone 7a/7b (Piedmont Region).
**Total Area:** 5,400 sq. ft.
**Orientation:** 90' length runs East-West to maximize southern sun exposure.
**Philosophy:** Calorie density and storage capability take precedence over variety. Perennials and vining crops are prioritized to reduce weeding (upkeep).

#### 1. Layout & Zoning (North to South)
To prevent shading, crops are arranged by height. All beds are 4' wide with 2' walking paths (included in square footage calculations).

*   **North Edge (60' strip, 5' deep): Windbreak & Tall Crops.**
    *   **Crop:** Mammoth Sunflowers (*Helianthus annuus*).
    *   **Function:** Seeds for oil/calories; stalks for trellising; windbreak.
*   **North-Central (60' x 20'): High Calorie Tubers.**
    *   **Crop:** Jerusalem Artichokes / Sunchokes (*Helianthus tuberosus*).
    *   **Function:** Extreme hardiness, high calorie yield, perennial (no replanting).
*   **Central (60' x 30'): Vining Calorie Crops.**
    *   **Crop:** Sweet Potatoes (*Ipomoea batatas*) and Winter Squash (*Cucurbita moschata* 'Waltham Butternut').
    *   **Function:** Ground cover suppresses weeds; high storage potential.
*   **South-Central (60' x 15'): Protein & Nitrogen Fixers.**
    *   **Crop:** Pole Beans (*Phaseolus vulgaris*) and Peanuts (*Arachis hypogaea*).
    *   **Function:** Beans climb sunflower stalks; Peanuts fix nitrogen; high protein/fat.
*   **South Edge (60' strip, 10' deep): Winter Greens & Forage.**
    *   **Crop:** Collard Greens (*Brassica oleracea*) and Purslane (*Portulaca oleracea* - managed weed).
    *   **Function:** Winter nutrition (vitamins/minerals) when roots are stored.
*   **Perimeter Fence:** Thornless Blackberries (*Rubus* spp.).
    *   **Function:** Perennial fruit, security barrier.

#### 2. Crop Rationale (Durability & Maintenance)
*   **Jerusalem Artichokes:** Survive frost, drought, and neglect. Tubers stay in ground until needed. *Warning: Invasive. Must be contained within the block.*
*   **Sweet Potatoes:** Vines choke out weeds. Disease resistant varieties selected.
*   **Winter Squash:** Hard skin allows 6+ month storage without electricity.
*   **Collards:** Survive Piedmont winters; yield increases after frost.
*   **Sunflowers:** Self-seeding if allowed; drought tolerant.

#### 3. Nutritional Analysis & Deficiencies
This plan prioritizes macronutrients (Carbs, Protein, Fat). Micronutrients are secondary but addressed via specific crops.

**Likely Nutrient Deficiencies:**
1.  **Vitamin B12:** No reliable plant source.
    *   *Non-Trade Source:* Consumption of soil bacteria on unwashed root vegetables (risky), fermentation of beans/vegetables (creates trace B12 analogs, unreliable), or insect consumption (grubs/beetles found in soil/compost).
2.  **Vitamin D:** No plant source.
    *   *Non-Trade Source:* Direct sun exposure (15-30 mins daily).
3.  **Omega-3 Fatty Acids:** Sunflowers and Peanuts are high in Omega-6.
    *   *Non-Trade Source:* Purslane (high in ALA Omega-3). Allow to grow as ground cover in bean/peanut beds.
4.  **Calcium:**
    *   *Non-Trade Source:* Bone char from animal remains (if any), or consumption of small fish/crayfish if water source exists. Otherwise, Collard Greens (high bioavailability calcium).
5.  **Iron:**
    *   *Non-Trade Source:* Cook in cast iron cookware (leaches iron into food). Pair with Vitamin C (Sunflower sprouts/Wild berries) to increase absorption.

#### 4. Pest Prevention Plan (Low Maintenance)
*   **Deer:** 60'x90' is a high-value target. A 7-8' fence is required. If unavailable, plant blackberries densely on the perimeter as a thorny deterrent.
*   **Squash Vine Borer:** Wrap the bottom 12" of squash stems with aluminum foil or row cover at planting.
*   **Potato/Sweet Potato Beetles:** Hand-pick adults in the morning and drop into soapy water. Rotate crop locations annually (move Sweet Potatoes to Sunflower bed next year).
*   **General Insects:** Diatomaceous Earth (DE) applied around plant bases. It is cheap, non-toxic to humans, and kills exoskeleton pests.
*   **Weeds:** Heavy mulching (straw/leaves) 6" deep. Vining crops (Sweet Potato/Squash) will suppress remaining weeds.

#### 5. Calorie Estimate (Year 1 Conservative Yield)
*Note: Year 1 yields are lower due to soil establishment. Estimates assume 50% of mature potential.*

| Crop | Area (sq. ft.) | Yield (lbs) | Cal/lb | Total Calories |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Sweet Potatoes** | 1,500 | 1,500 | 390 | 585,000 |
| **Jerusalem Artichokes**| 1,000 | 2,000 | 320 | 640,000 |
| **Winter Squash** | 1,000 | 1,000 | 150 | 150,000 |
| **Peanuts/Beans/Sunflower**| 1,000 | 400 (dry weight) | 2,500* | 1,000,000 |
| **Collards/Greens** | 500 | 1,000 | 50 | 50,000 |
| **Blackberries** | Perimeter | 200 | 200 | 40,000 |
| **Purslane (Forage)** | Intercrop | 100 | 200 | 20,000 |
| **TOTAL** | **5,400** | | | **2,485,000** |

*\*Note: Peanuts/Sunflower seeds are calorie dense (2,500+ cal/lb), but yield per sq ft is low compared to tubers. The 400 lbs dry weight is an optimistic aggregate for low-maintenance.*

**Total Estimated Calories:** 2,485,000 cal/year.
**Human Requirement (2 People):** 1,825,000 cal/year (2,500 cal/person/day).
**Status:** **Surplus (Theoretical).**
*Reality Check:* Post-harvest loss (rot, pests in storage) typically consumes 20-30% of root crops.
**Adjusted Usable Calories:** ~1,740,000 cal/year.
**Deficit:** ~85,000 cal/year.

#### 6. Alternate Suggestions for Shortfall
The theoretical surplus is erased by storage loss and the high energy expenditure of farming. To ensure survival:
1.  **Small Livestock:** Introduce 2 meat rabbits. They convert forage/weeds into high-protein, high-fat meat efficiently. Requires minimal space (hutches on North side).
2.  **Foraging Expansion:** Expand caloric foraging outside the 60'x90 block. Acorns (leached for tannins) and Persimmons are abundant in the Piedmont fall.
3.  **Insect Protein:** Farm mealworms in storage bins. They eat crop waste and provide high protein/fat.

#### 7. Huel Calculation (Bridge to Harvest)
**Current Date:** December 1st.
**Next Main Harvest:** Sweet Potatoes and Squash are harvested before the first hard frost, typically **October 1st**.
**Duration:** 10 Months (304 Days).
**Assumption:** During the growing season (Dec-Oct), the farm provides negligible *calories* (greens provide vitamins, not energy). You must bridge the entire caloric gap until the stored crops are cured and ready.

*   **Daily Caloric Need (2 People):** 5,000 calories.
*   **Total Calories Needed:** 5,000 cal/day * 304 days = 1,520,000 calories.
*   **Huel Specs:** 400 cal/serving * 17 servings/bag = 6,800 calories/bag.
*   **Bags Required:** 1,520,000 / 6,800 = 223.52 bags.
